sentences.text: Pervushovisaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur that reached a total length of 5.8 meters.
The animal possessed a straight rostrum, or snout, which gave its head a distinct profile.
Its teeth featured straight, non-recurved crowns, differing from the hooked shapes seen in some other marine reptiles.
Distinctive skull features included foramina along the ventral premaxillary-maxillary suture and a wide supranarial wing on the nasal bone.
The lower jaw showed a robust splenial protruding from the outside, with a root having a quadrangular cross-section where cementum formed prominent 90-degree angles.
Additionally, the species had a secondarily closed naris surrounded by small openings.
An elongated anterior process of the maxilla extended forward to reach the level of the nasal bone.
The genus Pervushovisaurus was formally described by Arkhangelsky in 1998.
The type species, P. bannovkensis, is known exclusively from the partial skull holotype SGU 104a/24.
Earlier, a specimen found in the La Penthiève Beds of France was described in 1882 by Henri Émile Sauvage.
In 2016, this specimen was referred to Pervushovisaurus, having previously been allied with Ichthyosaurus since 1846.
To date, there are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of this animal.
Pervushovisaurus was originally classified as a subgenus of Platypterygius but was later elevated to full generic rank due to distinct features.
It belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Within that family, it is classified within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
Pervushovisaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous, specifically the Cenomanian stage, approximately 100 to 94 million years ago.
However, the broader time range for the genus extends from the Albian to the Cenomanian, between 113.2 and 93.9 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in the Saratov Oblast in western Russia.
It inhabited the Saratov region of western Russia during this period.
Fossils of Pervushovisaurus have also been found in the La Penthiève Beds of France and the Cambridge area of the United Kingdom.
